transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been doing things at work and school that don’t really make sense. Like, I’ll line receipts across the floor, or tap the calculator in sets of nine. Sometimes I just end up standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I’m okay. It’s starting to worry me.
Do these actions, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, feel like something you have to do, even if you don’t want to?

Yeah… kind of. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it normally. I’ll just start lining the receipts up or tapping the calculator in nines, and even if part of me thinks it’s weird or I should stop, I keep doing it. Same with standing by the copier with my hands up — I don’t really know why I’m doing it until someone says something.
Do these actions make you feel anxious or upset, or do they happen without you feeling any particular emotion about them?

It’s not really anxiety, at least not at first. It more just happens, like I’ll be lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in nines before I really think about it. Then I might feel embarrassed or worried after someone notices, like when I’m standing by the copier with my hands up and they ask if I’m okay.
When you're doing these things, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, do you realize at the time that they don’t make sense, or does it feel like it needs to happen that way?

At the time, it kind of feels like it needs to happen that way. Like with the receipts, I’ll just start putting them across the floor, or with the calculator I keep tapping in sets of nine. I don’t really stop and think, “this makes no sense,” until after, or until someone notices—like when I’m standing by the copier with my hands up and they ask if I’m okay.
When you feel like you have to line up the receipts or tap the calculator in sets of nine, are you having a thought or feeling that something bad will happen if you don’t do it a certain way?

I don’t think it’s like… “something bad will happen.” I haven’t really noticed a specific thought like that. It’s more just this feeling that I’m supposed to do it that way, and I keep going until I’m stopped or I snap out of it.
Before you start lining up receipts or tapping the calculator in sets of nine, do you feel any kind of physical sensation or inner tension that gets relieved when you do the behavior?

I don’t really notice a physical feeling beforehand, like tension building up or anything. It’s more that I just start doing it—lining the receipts out, tapping the calculator in nines, or standing there by the copier with my hands up—and then I realize later it doesn’t really make sense.

Before you start doing these behaviors, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, do you have any particular thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that you can’t seem to get rid of?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed a specific thought or picture in my head before it happens. It’s more like I just kind of start doing it, and then later I realize I was stuck on it.
While you're doing these behaviors—like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator—do you have any thought that they might be strange, unnecessary, or something you shouldn't be doing?

Yeah… sometimes while I’m doing it, I kind of realize it looks strange, like standing by the copier with my hands up or spreading receipts out across the floor. But in the moment I don’t always stop right away. It’s like I’m caught in it until someone says something or I snap out of it.

Before you start doing these behaviors, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, do you ever feel a strange or uncomfortable sensation in your body that seems to go away only after you do the behavior?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed any weird body feeling that builds up and then goes away after I do it. It’s more like I just start doing it, and I don’t really know why.

Do you feel that you have to do these behaviors, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, in order to feel 'just right' or to prevent something uncomfortable from happening, even if you can’t explain exactly what that something is?

Not really like that. I don’t feel like something bad will happen if I don’t do it, and it’s not exactly to make things feel “just right.” I just end up doing these things that don’t make much sense, like lining the receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in nines, and I don’t really know why until someone points it out.
